result.summary: Pausanias finishes the career of Agesilaus, then covers his successors Archidamus, Agis and Eudamidas, including the Phocian seizure of Delphi. He then begins a road tour north of Sparta, describing sanctuaries at Scotitas, Caryæ, Sellasia and Thornax.

scenes.title: Agesilaus' later campaigns and death
scenes.summary: Agesilaus campaigns around Corinth, Ætolia and Egypt. He dies on the voyage home and is buried with great honour.
scenes.stakes: Agesilaus risks his army and, in old age, his life on foreign campaigns.

scenes.title: Archidamus and later Spartan kings
scenes.summary: Archidamus helps the Phocians at Delphi, saves Delphi from destruction and dies in Italy. His sons and successors are briefly noted.
scenes.stakes: Delphi and its people face destruction; Archidamus risks his reputation and later his life.

scenes.title: Road tour: Scotitas to Thornax
scenes.summary: Pausanias describes shrines and monuments along the roads north of Sparta, including Caryæ, Sellasia and Thornax.

alias_notes.explanation: Epithet meaning 'dark', giving the place its name.

notable_quotes.reason: Pausanias openly condemns taking sacred money and aiding the plunderers of Delphi.

analysis.text: Pausanias judges rulers by piety: aiding temple robbers is blamed, while saving Delphi is praised, and Archidamus' death is explained as Apollo's wrath.
The passage covers Sparta's decline from Agesilaus through the Sacred War and Macedonian dominance, before turning to a topographical tour.

fun_facts.text: Pausanias' Spartan road descriptions are valuable to archaeologists for locating Laconian sanctuaries.

language_notes.text: The Hyacinthia was a Spartan festival at Amyclæ honouring Hyacinthus and Apollo; Spartans were bound to attend, even on campaign.
"Mercenary aid" means paid troops; the sense is that offers of help came, the Thebans being at war with the Phocians.
"Deprecated" here means argued against and averted, not merely disapproved.
Tarentum was a Spartan colony in southern Italy; the "barbarians" are the native Italian peoples fighting it.
Scotitas is Greek for "dark"; Pausanias gives an etymology from Zeus's title rather than the oak shade.
Sellasia was where Cleomenes was defeated by the Achæans and Macedonians in 222 BC, ending Spartan power.

context_notes.text: Iphicrates was an Athenian general famed for his light troops, who destroyed a Spartan regiment near Corinth in 390 BC.
The Phocians' seizure of Delphi began the Sacred War (356–346 BC), in which they used temple treasure to pay mercenaries.
Hercules is said to have killed Hippocoon and his sons after they drove out Tyndareus and killed his kinsman.

literary_notes.text: Pausanias intrudes with a personal moral judgment, condemning the use of sacred money, which shows his piety.
The death abroad and the unburied body, attributed to Apollo's wrath, suggest divine punishment for Archidamus's earlier dealings with Delphi's plunderers.
